description: Starter content: ransomware preparation, credential theft, persistence, execution and defence evasion. Rules marked audit record hits without alerting until their false-positive rate is known.

behaviour_rules.name: Volume shadow copies deleted
behaviour_rules.description: vssadmin deleting or shrinking shadow copies, the first step of most ransomware.

behaviour_rules.name: Shadow copies deleted through WMI
behaviour_rules.description: wmic or PowerShell deleting Win32_ShadowCopy objects.

behaviour_rules.name: Windows recovery disabled
behaviour_rules.description: bcdedit switching off automatic repair, which ransomware does before encrypting.

behaviour_rules.name: Backup catalog deleted
behaviour_rules.description: wbadmin deleting the backup catalog or system state backups.

behaviour_rules.name: Many files renamed by one process
behaviour_rules.description: 30 renames within a minute by the same process, in watched folders: typical of encryption.

behaviour_rules.name: LSASS dumped with comsvcs.dll
behaviour_rules.description: rundll32 calling comsvcs MiniDump, a common way to steal credentials from memory.

behaviour_rules.name: LSASS dumped with ProcDump
behaviour_rules.description: Sysinternals ProcDump pointed at lsass.

behaviour_rules.name: Mimikatz commands
behaviour_rules.description: Mimikatz module syntax on a command line.

behaviour_rules.name: Credential hives saved
behaviour_rules.description: reg.exe saving the SAM, SECURITY or SYSTEM hive, to crack offline.

behaviour_rules.name: Shadow password file copied
behaviour_rules.description: Copying, encoding or sending /etc/shadow.

behaviour_rules.name: Program added to a Run key
behaviour_rules.description: A new value under a Run or RunOnce key starts a program at every sign-in.

behaviour_rules.name: Scheduled task created from a user folder
behaviour_rules.description: schtasks /create running something from Temp, AppData, Public or ProgramData.

behaviour_rules.name: systemd service added
behaviour_rules.description: A new unit file under /etc/systemd/system.

behaviour_rules.name: Crontab changed
behaviour_rules.description: System or user crontabs created or modified.

behaviour_rules.name: SSH authorized keys changed
behaviour_rules.description: A key added to someone's authorized_keys gives lasting access.

behaviour_rules.name: Library preload hijack
behaviour_rules.description: /etc/ld.so.preload makes every program load a library: rootkits use it.

behaviour_rules.name: Service created from a user folder
behaviour_rules.description: sc.exe create with the binary in Temp, AppData or Public.

process.name: sc.exe
process.command_line: sc create svc binpath= C:\Users\Public\s.exe start= auto

behaviour_rules.name: Encoded PowerShell command
behaviour_rules.description: PowerShell run with a long base64 -EncodedCommand, which hides what it does.

behaviour_rules.name: certutil used to download
behaviour_rules.description: certutil -urlcache fetching a file, a common living-off-the-land download.

behaviour_rules.name: Download piped into a shell
behaviour_rules.description: curl or wget output run straight by a shell.

behaviour_rules.name: Defender protection switched off
behaviour_rules.description: Set-MpPreference turning off real-time, behaviour or download scanning.

behaviour_rules.name: Event logs cleared
behaviour_rules.description: wevtutil cl or Clear-EventLog erasing the Windows logs.

behaviour_rules.name: Linux audit trail tampered with
behaviour_rules.description: Audit rules deleted, or shell history wiped.

behaviour_rules.name: Office app started a shell
behaviour_rules.description: Word, Excel, PowerPoint or Outlook starting a command shell or script host: usually a malicious document.

behaviour_rules.name: Reverse shell one-liner
behaviour_rules.description: A shell wired to a network socket.

behaviour_rules.name: Connection to a mining or C2 port
behaviour_rules.description: Outbound connections to ports used by miners and common C2 defaults.

behaviour_rules.name: Known rootkit module loaded
behaviour_rules.description: A Linux kernel module with the name of a public rootkit.
